solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Winning gamble — result!

blocks.note: a side that is up is ahead, winning
a shot is an attempt or punt, a gamble

explanation.surface: A punter celebrates a bet that has come off.
explanation.definitionFit: The upshot is the final outcome or consequence of events, a standard synonym.

clue.text: Book one has expert on cheese

blocks.note: a pro is a professional, an expert
vol is the abbreviation for volume
taken as written

explanation.surface: Volume one of a book contains an expert's take on cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so the expert comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Provolone is a mild Italian stretched-curd cheese made from cow's milk.

clue.text: Move south and north touring old US city

indicators.note: moving letters around puts them in a new order
a tour goes around a place, so the jumbled letters surround the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written
compass abbreviation
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A traveller heads south then north on a tour of an old American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South' reads as a direction to move in, but it is the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Houston is a major city in Texas in the United States, home of NASA's mission control.

clue.text: Draw string

blocks.note: first meaning: a match with no winner
second meaning: to fasten with a cord

explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw string' reads as a drawstring cord; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a game ending level and also to bind or knot something with cord.

clue.text: Brown has muzzled dog, keeping it quiet

indicators.note: a muzzle closes round a mouth, so the colour word wraps around what follows
keeping something means holding it inside, so the dog word holds the next piece

blocks.note: tan is a light brown
a cur is a mongrel dog
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone called Brown silences a noisy dog by muzzling it.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: the dog keeps 'it', and the colour muzzles the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A taciturn person says very little, reserved and uncommunicative in manner.

clue.text: With all players expressing disapproval, sending off no good

indicators.note: sending off removes a player from the field, so those letters are dismissed

blocks.note: tutting is clicking the tongue in disapproval
NG is the abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: A referee disapproves of everyone on the pitch and sends off an incompetent player.
explanation.walkthrough: The football picture hides a musical term; NG is removed from TUTTING.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutti is an Italian musical direction meaning the whole orchestra plays together.

clue.text: Furniture item, rope securing pedal?

indicators.note: securing something means holding it fast, so the rope word holds the next phrase inside

blocks.note: a cable is a thick rope
pedal as an adjective means of feet, as in pedal extremities

explanation.surface: Someone ties a rope round a bicycle pedal.
explanation.walkthrough: Pedal looks like a noun (bike part) but is the adjective meaning relating to the feet, giving OF FEET inside C...ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A coffee table is a low table placed in front of a sofa in a living room.

clue.text: Laugh, glugging whiskey in state of excitement

indicators.note: glugging is drinking down, so the laugh word takes in the drink

blocks.note: a titter is a nervous laugh
Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone laughs while gulping whiskey, getting worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: W goes inside TITTER after T.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a twitter is to be in a nervous flutter or agitated state.

clue.text: Measure sovereign

blocks.note: first meaning: a straight edge marked for measuring
second meaning: a monarch who governs

explanation.walkthrough: 'Measure sovereign' looks like weighing a gold coin; the words are two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a marked strip for measuring length and a king or queen who reigns.

clue.text: Greek character in second statue?

indicators.note: one thing placed in another is enclosed by it

blocks.note: a second is a brief moment
nu is the thirteenth letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek figure appears briefly, like a living statue.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark is there because a statue is only one kind of the thing defined.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue erected to commemorate someone is one example of a public memorial structure.

clue.text: Fancy horse that’s hugging rails initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the preceding word
to hug is to wrap arms around, so the horse word encloses the kept letter

blocks.note: a filly is a young female horse
first letter of rails

explanation.surface: A racegoer fancies a horse that keeps close to the running rails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy horse' reads as a verb and its object; fancy is in fact the adjective defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Frilly clothing is decorated with ruffles and trimmings, so ornate and elaborate.

clue.text: Place no longer functions, decorate building on high street?

blocks.note: to post someone is to place or station them
a machine that is off is not working
to ice a cake is to decorate it

explanation.surface: A defunct local amenity is spruced up while it no longer works.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface laments closures of high-street services, which the answer is a famous example of.
explanation.definitionFit: Post offices are typical premises found in a British town's main shopping street.

clue.text: Relative Fleming, say, rubbed out in Russian fiction novel

indicators.note: rubbing out erases, so those letters are removed from the text that follows
novel means new, so the remaining letters take a new order

blocks.note: Ian Fleming created James Bond; say marks the name as an example
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Bond author is erased from a Russian novel.
explanation.walkthrough: IAN comes out of RUSSIAN, leaving eleven letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A first cousin is the child of one's aunt or uncle, a family member.

clue.text: Wrong pace after retirement

indicators.note: to retire is to withdraw or go back, so the word is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: a trot is a running pace

explanation.surface: Someone slows the pace wrongly after giving up work.
explanation.definitionFit: In law a tort is a civil wrong for which damages can be claimed.

clue.text: Something soft on the ground

blocks.note: first meaning: fine fluffy feathers
second meaning: fallen or floored

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a soft landing; the two phrases are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a bird's fine under-feathers and also describes a boxer floored or a plane landed.

clue.text: OK, one has cut source of fibre — half one’s loaf?

indicators.note: a thing that cuts into something sits inside it

blocks.note: right as in all right, OK
bran is a dietary source of fibre
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A baker is fine with halving a fibre-rich loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: Loaf is slang for head, as in 'use your loaf', and the brain has two hemispheres; I goes inside BRAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The right hemisphere is one of two halves of the brain inside a person's head.

clue.text: Fish swimming around hooks

indicators.note: to hook is to catch, so the phrase catches the answer within it

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A fish swimming about takes the bait.
explanation.walkthrough: Hooks looks like a noun, fishing tackle, but it is a verb meaning catches.
explanation.definitionFit: The gar is a long-snouted freshwater fish of North America with needle-like teeth.

clue.text: Clever voiding of guarantee, unions I suspect defending it

indicators.note: voiding empties out, so only the two end letters remain
something suspect is dodgy, so the letters are not to be trusted in this order
defenders stand round what they protect, so the jumbled letters surround the kept pair

blocks.note: first and last letters of guarantee
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone suspects unions of defending a cancelled guarantee by a clever ruse.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingenious means inventive and resourceful, showing originality and skill.

clue.text: Courage is lacking in this mug, lovely chap?

indicators.note: lacking means without, so those two letters are taken out of the next word

blocks.note: heart means bravery
taken as written, before losing two letters
the letters removed
to mug someone is to rob them

explanation.surface: A bruiser who robs people lacks real courage, despite being called lovely.
explanation.walkthrough: Mug looks like a face or cup; here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A heartthrob is a handsome man whom many admirers find attractive and swoon over.

clue.text: Italian maestro edges away from junction, heading for Italy

indicators.note: with its edges gone, the word loses its first and last letters
a heading is at the top, so the first letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: a crossing is a junction of roads or rails
first letter of Italy

explanation.surface: An Italian conductor edges away from a road junction, heading for home.
explanation.definitionFit: Gioachino Rossini was the Italian composer of The Barber of Seville and William Tell.

clue.text: Writer of silent work shut up

blocks.note: first meaning: the American composer of 4'33", a piece of silence
second meaning: to confine, as an animal

explanation.surface: A writer of silent work is told to be quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shut up' sounds like an order to be quiet but means to confine. John Cage wrote 4'33", in which the performer plays nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname names the composer of a silent piece, and the verb means to imprison behind bars.

clue.text: English accessing castle, tipsy — is one hammered?

indicators.note: a tipsy person is unsteady, so the letters stagger into a new order
accessing means getting inside, so the letter goes within the others

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Englishman gets into a castle drunk and asks whether someone is hammered.
explanation.walkthrough: Hammered looks like slang for drunk, matching tipsy; it actually describes an instrument whose hammers strike metal bars.
explanation.definitionFit: A celesta is a keyboard instrument in which felt hammers strike steel plates, heard in the Sugar Plum Fairy dance.

clue.text: A musical, but not a book

indicators.note: but not means excluding, so the following letter is removed from the show name

blocks.note: taken as written
Lloyd Webber's long-running musical
the letter removed

explanation.surface: Someone recommends a musical rather than reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not a book' seems to reject reading; actually book is the definition, and only the letter a is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: The Acts of the Apostles is the fifth book of the New Testament in the Bible.

clue.text: Island oddly curved then

indicators.note: oddly means taking the odd-numbered letters, first, third, fifth and so on

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters

explanation.surface: An island's coastline curves in an odd way.
explanation.definitionFit: Crete is the largest Greek island, in the Mediterranean south of the mainland.

clue.text: About to fail — like one’s indicators?

blocks.note: first meaning: malfunctioning, on its last legs
second meaning, cryptic: car turn signals flash on and off

explanation.surface: A worried driver suspects the car is failing.
explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is a whimsical literal reading of the idiom, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes equipment working erratically and close to breaking down.

clue.text: Skyscraper, say, erected on what?

indicators.note: in a down clue, erected means set upright, so the letters read from the bottom up

blocks.note: re means on or concerning
wot is a jocular spelling of what

explanation.surface: Someone puzzles over what a skyscraper was built on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks a skyscraper as one example of the defined thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A skyscraper is a very tall building, an example of a tower rising high above its surroundings.

clue.text: Fines collected, last of those stuffed into trousers

indicators.note: last of points to the final letter of the next word
stuffed into means packed inside something

blocks.note: Levi's are a brand of jeans
final letter of those

explanation.surface: Collected fines are crammed into a pair of trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: E goes inside LEVIS between the I and the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Levies are charges imposed and gathered by an authority, so sums of money taken as penalties or taxes.

clue.text: Course that’s hard in Notts town

indicators.note: one thing in another is surrounded by it

blocks.note: Worksop is a market town in Nottinghamshire
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A demanding course is held in a Nottinghamshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Notts is the usual short form of Nottinghamshire, an English county in the Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: A workshop is a short practical training session or class on a particular subject.

clue.text: Mythical bird bigger, so gigantic ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so the final letter of each word is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A legendary bird is described as huge and growing.
explanation.definitionFit: The roc is a giant bird of Arabian legend, said to carry off elephants in the Sinbad stories.

clue.text: Ask for private trainee

blocks.note: to beg is to ask earnestly
inner thoughts are private ones

explanation.surface: A soldier's request on behalf of a new recruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Private suggests a soldier, which fits trainee nicely, but it is an adjective here.
explanation.definitionFit: A beginner is a novice just starting to learn, as an apprentice or learner is.

clue.text: Old carriage I observed in pursuit

indicators.note: something observed in a place is seen inside it

blocks.note: a chase is a pursuit
taken as written

explanation.surface: A narrator spots a horse-drawn carriage in a chase scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaise was a light two-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle for one or two people, now historical.
